06be81c33f1d026ac8e26c32e65159047407f345.overall_assessment: The virtual-asset system demonstrates strong compliance with most HKMA/SFC supervisory requirements, effectively supporting client asset protection and market integrity through modular compliance controls and identity anchoring mechanisms. However, key gaps remain in the comprehensive on-chain registration and recordkeeping of licensed persons, particularly regarding updating identity registries and capturing critical license event attributes.

findings.title: Incomplete on-chain register of licensed persons due to missing identity update function
findings.explanation: The system includes an on-chain identity registry (token.identityRegistry()), but lacks the essential updateIdentity(address,address,uint16[]) function to modify licensee identity data post-registration. Under SFO (Cap.571) §53ZRH(1), maintaining an up-to-date register of licensed persons is mandatory for ongoing supervisory oversight. Without this update capability, the registry cannot be reliably maintained, risking insufficient audit trail for licensing changes and weakening the control environment against unauthorized or obsolete license data.
findings.recommendation: Implement and deploy a secure updateIdentity(address,address,uint16[]) function within the identity registry contract to enable authorized amendments of licensee data. Ensure associated event logging for transparency and audit readiness.

findings.title: Absence of central entity identification claim function
findings.explanation: The identity registry lacks the identity(address) function, which is required by SFO (Cap.571) §53ZRH(2)(a)(iii) to anchor a central claim identifying licensed entities. This creates a gap in the authoritative source of entity identity on-chain, impairing the reliability of licensing claims and potentially complicating regulatory verification and enforcement actions. A robust identity claim function is critical for supervisory confidence in the identity data presented.
findings.recommendation: Introduce the identity(address) function within the identity registry contract to return comprehensive identity claims for licensed entities. Maintain event logging for identity queries to support audit and supervisory monitoring.

findings.title: Missing on-chain capture of licence grant timestamp
findings.explanation: No event named IdentityRegistered is emitted, which is mandated under SFO (Cap.571) §53ZRH(2)(a)(iv) to record the timestamp when a licence is granted. This omission prevents clear, immutable evidence of licensing timing, which is crucial for regulatory audit trails and ensuring license validity periods are enforceable. Absence of grant timestamp jeopardizes supervisory ability to verify licensing status during compliance checks.
findings.recommendation: Add an IdentityRegistered event that captures the license grant timestamp and relevant licensee parameters upon initial registration. This event should be emitted reliably to facilitate transparent and tamper-proof event logging for supervisory verification.

findings.title: Insufficient ongoing record of customer identity and activity due to missing identity query function
findings.explanation: While the registry supports identity verification status through isVerified(address), it lacks the identity(address) function required under AMLO Schedule 2 §6 to maintain a comprehensive ongoing record of customer identity details and associated activities. This gap impairs ongoing due diligence and monitoring, increasing risks of non-compliance with regulatory mandates to keep accurate customer identity records. Supervisors will view this as a serious deficiency in KYC governance and audit readiness.
findings.recommendation: Develop and deploy the identity(address) function that returns detailed customer identity claims to enable robust recordkeeping and ongoing monitoring. Align this with event auditing mechanisms to support supervisory assurance and client asset protection.

findings.title: Compliant recording of licence conditions with effective dates

findings.recommendation: Continue maintaining this functionality with rigorous testing and event monitoring to ensure ongoing integrity of licensing condition records.

findings.title: Adequate representation of licence suspension status on-chain

findings.title: Effective role-based control over virtual asset transfers

This role gating is critical to preventing unauthorized transactions and ensuring only verified parties engage in virtual asset transfers, thereby mitigating money laundering and illicit finance risks.
findings.recommendation: Ensure ongoing monitoring and testing of role gating logic to prevent bypass and confirm operational integrity.

findings.title: Strong client asset safeguards implemented via modular compliance

b077fa8a44b101abe8d884cfab16405a77bcabd4.overall_assessment: The examined virtual asset smart contract exhibits substantial non-compliance with HKMA/SFC AML and licensing standards, particularly concerning the maintenance of on-chain registers of licensed persons, representation of suspension status, and ongoing customer identity verification. While modular compliance controls appear robust, critical identity registry and freeze functionality are missing, presenting material supervisory risks.

findings.title: On-chain register lacks identityRegistry() function
findings.explanation: The smart contract ABI does not expose the identityRegistry() function, which is essential under SFO (Cap.571) §53ZRH(1) for maintaining an on-chain register of licensed persons. This absence impairs the ability to track authorized entities on-chain, undermining regulatory transparency and auditability. Without a reliable register, the licensee risks non-compliance with licensing obligations, reducing the HKMA/SFC's oversight effectiveness and increasing associated supervisory risks. Remediation requires implementing and exposing the identityRegistry() function per ERC-3643 to ensure a robust and accessible register of licensed persons with appropriate event logging and data integrity controls for audit readiness.

findings.title: Missing isVerified(address) function for customer identity verification
findings.explanation: The control to verify ongoing customer identity & activity, mandated under AMLO Schedule 2 §6, is not supported due to the absent isVerified(address) function in the identity registry interface. This function is critical to confirm that customers remain verified to prevent illicit transactions. Its absence introduces significant regulatory and business risks including failure to detect unverified actors, exposing the virtual asset provider to AML breaches and potential enforcement. The gap indicates a weakness in ongoing KYC due diligence and client protection governance. Remediation involves implementing the isVerified(address) method to support continuous verification status checks, coupled with secure event logging for supervisory review and audit trail completeness.
findings.recommendation: Develop and deploy the isVerified(address) function within the identity registry smart contract. This function must allow permissioned modules to query verified status reliably and emit events reflecting status changes for audit readiness.

findings.title: Absent token.compliance() method disables transfer role gating
findings.explanation: Under AMLO Schedule 2 §13A(1), role-based gating of virtual asset transfers is obligatory to restrict transfers to authorized participants and ensure compliance with AML requirements. The missing token.compliance() function means that the token contract cannot reference or invoke the modular compliance logic to enforce transfer restrictions, creating a major regulatory control gap. Without this linkage, unauthorized transfers may occur unchecked, threatening market integrity and client asset protection. This is regarded as a failure to implement appropriate transaction screening controls. The contract must expose the token.compliance() method to integrate with compliance modules enforcing role gating and verification.
findings.recommendation: Implement the token.compliance() method returning the compliance module address to enable enforcement of transfer restrictions. Ensure compliance logic is invoked on each transfer for role gating and that relevant events capturing transfer decisions are emitted for supervisory oversight.
